verses.sanskrit:
जनमेजय उवाच।
              अनुज्ञातांस्तान्विदित्वा सरत्नधनसञ्चयान्। पाण्डवान्धार्तराष्ट्राणां कथमासीन्मनस्तदा॥१॥
verses.english: Janamejaya said How did the sons of Dhritarashtra feel when they came to know that the Pandavas had with Dhritarashtra's permission left Hastinapur with all their wealth and jewels?

verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              अनुज्ञातांस्तान्विदित्वा धृतराष्ट्रेण धीमता। राजन्दुःशासनः क्षिप्रं जगाम भ्रातरं प्रति॥२॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said O king, having learnt that the Pandavas had been commanded by the wise Dhritarashtra to return to their capital Dushasana soon went to his brother.

verses.sanskrit: दुर्योधनं समासाद्य सामात्यं भरतर्षभ। दुःखार्तो भरतश्रेष्ठ इदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥३॥
verses.english: O best of the Bharata race, having come before Duryodhana (sitting) with his counsellors he spoke thus in a sorrowful heart.
verses.bhavadeepa: धृतराष्ट्रेण यथाप्रतिज्ञं सुहृद्द्यूते कृतेऽपि पुरुषकाराद्बलवत्तरं दैवं कौरवान् सर्वभूपक्षयहेतौ अनुद्यूते प्रावर्तयदित्याह अनुज्ञातानिति ॥२॥

verses.sanskrit:
दुःशासन उवाच।
              दुःखेनैतत्समानीतं स्थविरो नाशयत्यसौ। शत्रुसाद्गमयद्द्रव्यं तद्बुध्यध्वं महारथाः॥४॥
verses.english: Dushasana said O great car-warrior, the old man has thrown away, what we earned with so much trouble. Know that he had made over the whole of that wealth to our enemies.
verses.bhavadeepa: भरतश्रेष्ठः भरतस्य दुर्योधनस्य दृष्ट्या श्रेष्ठः प्रशस्यतमो दुःशासनः ॥३॥

verses.sanskrit: अथ दुर्योधनः कर्णः शकुनिश्चापि सौबलः। मिथः सङ्गम्य सहिताः पाण्डवान्प्रतिमानिनः॥५॥
verses.english: King Duryodhana and the son of Subala, Shakuni, these two best of men only remained in that celestials Sabha (assembly-hall).
verses.bhavadeepa: स्थविरो वृद्ध इति साधिक्षेपमुक्तं शत्रुसात् शत्रुवशं गमयदगमयत्प्रापितवान् ॥४॥

verses.sanskrit: वैचित्रवीर्यं राजानं धृतराष्ट्रं मनीषिणम्। अभिगम्य त्वरायुक्ताः श्लक्ष्णं वचनमब्रुवन्॥६॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said Thereupon, Duryodhana, and Karna, all exceedingly proud and vain-being united together and wishing to counteract the Pandavas went in haste and saw the king Dhritarashtra, the son of Vichitravirya. They spoke to him these smooth and artful words.

verses.sanskrit:
दुर्योधन उवाच।
              न त्वयेदं श्रुतं राजन्यज्जगाद बृहस्पतिः। शक्रस्य नीतिं प्रवदन्विद्वान्देवपुरोहितः॥७॥
verses.english: Duryodhana said O king, have you not heard what the learned Brihaspati, the preceptor of the celestial, said on morals and politics when advising Shakra (Indra).

verses.sanskrit: सर्वोपायैर्निहन्तव्याः शत्रवः शत्रुसूदन। पुरा युद्धाद्बलाद्वापि प्रकुर्वन्ति तवाहितम्॥८॥
verses.english: O chastiser of foes, (he said), “Those enemies who always harm by force or stratagem should be destroyed by every means".
verses.bhavadeepa: त्वया इदं किं न श्रुतमिति काक्वा नञो योजना अपि तु श्रुतमेव ॥७॥

verses.sanskrit: ते वयं पाण्डवधनैः सर्वान्सम्पूज्य पार्थिवान्। यदि तान्योधयिष्यामः किं वै निः परिहास्यति॥९॥
verses.english: If we gratify with the wealth of his Pandavas, the kings of the world and then fight with the sons of Pandu, what reverse can overtake us?
verses.bhavadeepa: पुरा युद्धात् युद्धमकृत्वेत्यर्थः बलाद्युद्धेन वा ये अहितं कुर्वन्ति ते निहन्तव्या इति योजना ॥८॥

verses.sanskrit: अहीनाशीविषान्क्रुद्धान्नाशाय समुपस्थितान्। कृत्वा कण्ठे च पृष्ठे च कः समुत्स्रष्टुमर्हति॥१०॥
verses.english: When one places on his neck and back angry snakes full of venom, which has come to bring about his destruction, is it possible for him to take them off?

verses.sanskrit: आत्तशस्त्रा रथगताः कुपितास्तात पाण्डवाः। निःशेषं वः करिष्यन्ति क्रुद्धा ह्याशीविषा इव॥११॥
verses.english: O father, equipped with weapons and seated on cars, the Pandavas will annihilate us like angry and poisonous snakes.

verses.sanskrit: सन्नद्धो ह्यर्जुनो याति विधृत्य परमेषुधी। गाण्डीवं मुहुरादत्ते निःश्वसंश्च निरीक्षते॥१२॥
verses.english: Even now Arjuna, attired in armour and furnished with couple of quivers, is proceeding, frequently taking up the Gandiva (bow) and breathing hard and casting angry glances around.

verses.sanskrit: गदां गुर्वी समुद्यम्य त्वरितश्च वृकोदरः। स्वरथं योजयित्वाऽशु निर्यात इति नः श्रुतम्॥१३॥
verses.english: We are told that Vrikodara (Bhima), hastily ordering his chariot to be made ready and then riding on it, frequently whirling his heavy club is proceeding along.

verses.sanskrit: नकुलः खह्गमादाय चर्म चाप्यर्धचन्द्रवत्। सहदेवश्च राजा च चक्रुराकारमिङ्गितैः॥१४॥
verses.english: Nakula also is proceeding with the sword in his grasp and the semicircular shield in his hand; Sahadeva and the king (Yudhisthira) have made signs clearly indicating their intentions.

verses.sanskrit: ते त्वास्थाय रथान्सर्वे बहुशस्त्रपरिच्छदान्। अभिघ्नान्तो रथव्रातान्सेनायोगाय निर्ययुः॥१५॥
verses.english: Having ascended their cars which were full of all kings of weapons, they are all whipping their horses, (so that they might soon reach their capital) to assemble their forces.
verses.bhavadeepa: आकारम् अभिप्रायम् इङ्गितैश्चेष्टितैः चक्रुः आविश्चक्रुः कृ विक्षेपे इत्यस्य रूपम् ॥१४॥

verses.sanskrit: न क्षंस्यन्ते तथाऽस्माभिर्जातु विप्रकृता हि ते। द्रौपद्याश्च परिक्लेशं कस्तेषां क्षन्तुमर्हति॥१६॥
verses.english: Persecuted (as) they are (by us), they cannot forgive us for those injuries. Who is there amongst them who will be able to forgive the insult to Draupadi?

verses.sanskrit: पुनर्दिव्याम भद्रं ते वनवासाय पाण्डवैः। एवमेतान्वशे कर्तुं शक्ष्यामः पुरुषर्षभ॥१७॥
verses.english: O foremost of all men, be blessed. We shall again gamble with the Pandavas in order to send them to exile in the forest. We are able to bring them under our sway in this way.
verses.bhavadeepa: न क्षंस्यन्ते न क्षमां करिष्यन्ते । जातु कदाचित् । विप्रकृताः विकारं प्रापिताः तेषां मध्ये॥१६॥

verses.sanskrit: ते वा द्वादश वर्षाणि वयं वा द्यूतनिर्जिताः। प्रविशेम महारण्यमजिनैः प्रतिवासिताः॥१८॥
verses.english: Attired in skins, either they or we, having (first) been defeated at dice, shall go into the forest for twelve years.

verses.sanskrit: त्रयोदशं सजनेन अज्ञाताः प्रतिवत्सरम्। ज्ञाताश्च पुनरन्यानि वने वर्षाणि द्वादश॥१९॥
verses.english: The thirteenth year shall have to be spent in some inhabited country without being recognised. If recognised, an exile for another twelve years shall be the consequence(of such recognition).

verses.sanskrit: निवसेम वयं ते वा तथा द्यूतं प्रवर्तताम्। अक्षानुप्त्वा औनर्द्यूतमिदं कुर्वन्तु पाण्डवाः॥२०॥
verses.english: Either they or we shall live (according to this engagement). Let therefore the game begin. Throwing the dice, let the Pandavas once more play.

verses.sanskrit: एतत्कृत्यतमं राजन्नस्माकं भरतर्षभ। अयं हि शकुनिर्वेद सविद्यामक्षसंपदम्॥२१॥
verses.english: O best of Bharata race, O king, this is our highest duty. This Shakuni is highly proficient in the whole science of dice-playing.

verses.sanskrit: दृढमूलावयं राज्ये मित्राणि परिगृह्य च। सारवद्विपुलं सैन्यं सत्कृत्य च दुरासदम्॥२२॥
verses.english: We shall in the meantime be firmly rooted in the kingdom and making alliances (with other kings), we shall be able to get together a vast and invincible army and to keep them content.

verses.sanskrit: ते च त्रयोदशं वर्षं पारयिष्यन्ति चेद्व्रतम्। ज्येष्यामस्तान्वयं राजन्रोचतां ते परन्तप॥२३॥
verses.english: O king, O chastiser of foes, we shall then be able to defeat the Pandavas if they reappear. Let this plan recommend itself to you.

verses.sanskrit:
धृतराष्ट्र उवाच।
              तूर्णं प्रत्यानयस्वैतान्कामं व्यध्वगतानपि। आगच्छन्तु पुनर्द्यूतमिदं कुर्वन्तु पाण्डवाः॥२४॥
verses.english: Dhritarashtra said Then bring back the Pandavas, even if they have gone a great way off. Let them come and throw dice once again.

verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              ततो द्रोणः सोमदत्तो बाह्लीकश्चैव गौतमः। विदुरो द्रोणपुत्रश्च वैश्यापुत्रश्च वीर्यवान्॥२५॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said Thereupon, Drona, Somadatta, Vahlika, Goutama, the son of Drona, the powerful son of Vaishya (Vidura).

verses.sanskrit: भूरिश्रवाः शान्तनवो विकर्णश्च महारथः। मा द्यूतमित्यभाषन्त शमोस्त्विति च सर्वशः॥२६॥
verses.english: Bhurisrava,, Bhisma, and the mighty carwarrior Vikarna all said, “Let not the play commence. Let there be peace.”

verses.sanskrit: अकामानां च सर्वेषां सुहृदामर्थदर्शिनाम्। अकरोत्पाण्डवाह्वानं धृतराष्ट्रः सुतप्रियः॥२७॥
verses.english: But disregarding the counsels of all his wise friends and relatives, Dhritarashtra ever partial to his sons, (again) summoned the Pandavas.
